d.why: Tony Toscano is a real film critic credited as himself in Fantastic Four (2005), one of the media people around the team; a real person as themselves is out.
Jamie Little is a real sports reporter credited as herself in Fantastic Four (2005); a real person as themselves is out.
Kenny Bartram is a real freestyle motocross rider appearing under his own nickname 'Cowboy Kenny' in Fantastic Four (2005), a real person as himself with no part in the plot.
Dawn Chubai is a real TV host credited as herself in Rise of the Silver Surfer, a newsreader with no part in the plot; a real person as themselves is out.
Chris Gailus is a real news anchor credited as himself in Rise of the Silver Surfer, reading the news with no part in the plot; a real person as themselves is out.
Julie Angel is Johnny Storm's supermodel date at Reed and Sue's wedding in Rise of the Silver Surfer; she is on screen briefly and left behind when Johnny chases the Surfer, which changes nothing.
Giuliana Rancic (DePandi) is the real E! News reporter credited as herself, covering the wedding crowd in Rise of the Silver Surfer; a real person as themselves is out.
Nicole is one of the women Johnny brings to Reed's bachelor party in Rise of the Silver Surfer, with a line or two of flirting in one scene that changes nothing.
Cutter is one of Howard Saint's henchmen in The Punisher (2004), seen among Saint's men and killed in Castle's attack on the club, with no lines of his own or part in the story.
T.J. is Bobby Saint's bodyguard in The Punisher (2004), who pleads in one short scene that Bobby told him to stay behind before Howard kills him; the scene changes nothing in the plot.
Spoon is a Saint henchman in The Punisher (2004), one of the crew Castle kills at the club, with no lines or part of his own on screen.
Dante is one of Howard Saint's henchmen in The Punisher (2004), killed in Castle's assault on the club, with no lines or part of his own on screen.

Yuri Astrov, 'Mr. Ostroff', is the Russian arms dealer in the opening FBI sting of The Punisher (2004), with a few words ('We have deal?') in one scene; the story then turns on Bobby Saint's death, not on him.
Rick Elmhurst is a real person credited as himself in The Punisher (2004), with no part in the plot; a real person as themselves is out.
Carleth Keys is a real TV news reporter credited as herself in The Punisher (2004), reporting on the killings; a real person as themselves is out.
The Hydra Buyer is the Hydra agent Carson brings to the Yellowjacket sale in Ant-Man, knocked out by Scott; 'Hydra Buyer' is a job description, not a name.
The Writer is the journalist in Luis's story in Ant-Man who tells Sam Wilson about underground heroes and passes word on; 'Writer' is a job description, not a name.
Stoltz is the corrupt FBI agent on Jimmy Woo's team in Ant-Man and the Wasp who leaks to Sonny Burch, leads the raid that arrests Hank and Hope, and is killed by Ghost as he steals the lab for Burch.
Klaue's Mercenary is the bodyguard beside Klaue during the vibranium sale in Avengers: Age of Ultron, whose one line is 'Which ones?'; 'Klaue's Mercenary' is a job description, not a name.

Cameron Klein is the S.H.I.E.L.D. launch tech who refuses Rumlow's order to launch the Insight Helicarriers ('Captain's orders') in The Winter Soldier, then launches the lifeboats from Fury's Helicarrier at Sokovia in Age of Ultron.
Madame B. is the Red Room trainer who drives young Natasha through her training and the graduation ceremony in the vision of Avengers: Age of Ultron, speaking with her across the scene.
Gamora's mother hides with young Gamora and is killed by the Chitauri in one short Avengers: Infinity War flashback; 'Gamora's Mother' is a description, not a name, and the scene changes nothing.
The River Tribe Elder speaks for his tribe on the Wakandan council in Black Panther and Wakanda Forever; 'River Tribe Elder' is a title for a post, not a name.
The Merchant Tribe Elder argues on the Wakandan council that Wakanda needs a king, not a warrior, in Black Panther and Wakanda Forever; 'Merchant Tribe Elder' is a title for a post, not a name.
Limbani is Klaue's accomplice in Black Panther who poses as a paramedic to kill the guards in the museum heist, helps break Klaue out of the CIA, and is shot by Killmonger at the airfield.
Sope the Shaman gives Killmonger the Heart-Shaped Herb, refuses then is forced to burn the herb garden in Black Panther, and leads T'Challa's funeral rites in Wakanda Forever.

Zawavari is the Mining Tribe elder on the Wakandan council who scoffs at Killmonger's claim in Black Panther and, as elder statesman in Wakanda Forever, presses the council to choose a ruler and calls the challenge at the coronation.
The Mining Tribe Elder, Zawavari's successor, urges the council to give Namor what he asks in Wakanda Forever; 'Mining Tribe Elder' is a title for a post, not a name.
